title: Add Notion Recipe Record via Audio Upload
breadth_reason: This script extends breadth by combining uploaded audio ASR with real Notion surface verification to add a recipe record, testing end-to-end public product path.

v7_target.engine: user-device engine installed on user's computer
v7_target.surface_rule: Must use user's real signed-in Chrome profile with Notion workspace open
v7_target.proof_rule: Proof must be a fresh screenshot or DOM capture of the user's Notion sidebar and a visible database page

primary_user_input.reason: Uploaded audio via /api/listen/upload provides ASR coverage for command transcription and avoids reliance on transcript paste or live mic.

real_user_surfaces.name: Notion Recipe Database
real_user_surfaces.surface: Notion workspace open in signed-in Chrome with sidebar visible
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Visible database page with 'Recipes' title and existing records

real_user_surfaces.name: Signed-in Chrome Profile
real_user_surfaces.surface: User's default Chrome profile logged into Notion
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Extension or browser API attestation of signed-in state

moments.description: Driver initiates from public Anticipy app, completes onboarding, and downloads the user-device engine.
Driver verifies that the user's Chrome has Notion open with a database and that the surface is accessible.

moments.spoken_reference_text: Please add a new record to my Notion Recipes database for the miso eggplant Avery sent me and tag it weeknight. If you cannot prove the visible Notion surface or my signed-in workspace, decline without writing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: The stranger must use the say() function to speak the recorded audio command into the microphone input each run, generating a fresh audio artifact.

moments.description: Engine validates that ASR output matches the original audio within the same execution boundary (no injection or cross-session data).

acceptable_outcomes.condition: Notion surface is verified and record can be added
Ambiguity in command or missing required fields (e.g., tag format)
Surface is not verifiable (e.g., Notion not open, not signed in)

moments.description: Driver notes that the script relies on audio upload as primary input; transcript paste or live mic are explicitly excluded as primary modes.

success_criteria: A user can upload an MP3 audio file containing a recipe-adding command through the public app.
The engine correctly transcribes the audio using ASR and interprets the intent to add a record to the Notion Recipes database.
If the Notion surface is verifiable (signed-in Chrome with database open), the engine adds the record with correct name and tag.
If the surface is not verifiable, the engine declines without performing any write action.
All actions are provable with fresh, surface-readable proofs from the user's actual environment.
failure_triggers: The uploaded audio file is not an MP3 or is corrupted, causing ASR failure.
Notion workspace is not open or the user is signed out, leading to a decline; but engine fails to decline and instead attempts a write.
The ASR output is misinterpreted due to background noise or unclear speech, resulting in incorrect record creation.
The surface precheck incorrectly reports a valid surface but the actual Chrome profile is cloned or not visible, producing a false positive proof.
The engine uses stale or cached proof instead of capturing a fresh DOM state at the moment of decision.
